sources.label: Disciple of Varashta Djinn Video Guide

sections.title: Overview
paragraphs: Disciple of Varashta is a Sorceress ascendancy that binds two Djinns — Kelari and Ruzhan. They auto-attack nearby enemies, so mapping feels like playing a spellcaster while the Djinns do the damage. You step in with commands for burst and control.
The build scales as minion/command damage, not as your own spell damage. That is the key mental model: investing in minion and command scaling improves the Djinns far more than generic spell levels.

sections.title: Pros and Cons
pros: Very smooth mapping — the Djinns clear while you move.
Feels like a caster but benefits from minion/command scaling.
Two Djinns cover different elements, giving build flexibility.
Viable SSF once the required unique pieces are obtained.
cons: Bossing needs more buttons than mapping — commands are manual.
A Djinn can lose target or wander off in cluttered scenes.
Not a zero-gear SSF starter; some uniques are mandatory.
Your own defenses and the Djinns' survival are separate problems.

sections.title: Is This Build Right For You?
paragraphs: Pick Disciple of Varashta if you enjoy pet/command play but want caster-style pacing, and you are comfortable pressing commands during boss windows. It is not a fully passive build despite the auto-attacks.
SSF is realistic only after you secure the mandatory unique pieces. Do not expect to league-start it with nothing — verify which uniques are non-negotiable first.

steps.label: Campaign — Generic Sorceress
body: Level with a standard spell (e.g. Bonestorm or a lightning spell). The Djinns come online once you ascend Disciple of Varashta.

steps.label: Early Maps — Bind the Djinns
body: Allocate Disciple of Varashta, bind Kelari and Ruzhan, and start investing in minion/command scaling rather than raw spell levels.

sections.title: What Is Automatic vs Manual
paragraphs: Automatic: the Djinns choose targets and attack on their own during mapping. Manual: you issue commands for burst, control, and element switching on bosses. Understanding this split explains why mapping is relaxed but bossing is button-heavy.
A Djinn is not a mindless turret — it can lose line of sight in tight maps or wander. Keep fights in open space where possible and re-issue commands if a Djinn stalls.

sections.title: Mapping Loop
paragraphs: Walk into packs; the Djinns auto-clear. Only intervene with a command if a rare needs burst. This is the build's strongest mode.

sections.title: Boss Loop
paragraphs: Pre-load the right element on Ruzhan, issue burst commands on windows, and keep the Djinns alive with positioning. Expect to press several buttons per phase — this is not the mapping auto-clear.

steps.label: Bind Both Djinns
body: The ascendancy's payoff is commanding Kelari and Ruzhan. Confirm node names against the current client before respeccing.

body: Path through minion damage, command skill effect, and elemental notes. Generic spell levels help less than command scaling.

sections.title: SSF Reality Check
paragraphs: SSF is possible but not free. Separate gear into: vendor/campaign obtainable, common drops, craftable replacements, specific-unique required, and trade-only convenience. Only the 'required unique' tier blocks SSF — verify which pieces those are before committing.

sections.title: Content Fit
paragraphs: Best for mapping, bossing, and SSF-once-geared. Weak for players who want zero input, and for fights where the Djinns cannot keep line of sight.

sections.title: Community Questions

entries.label: Djinn survivability
entries.statement: Players report the Djinns can die or get stuck; they are not permanent invulnerable turrets.

entries.label: Scaling
entries.statement: Community consensus: minion and command-skill scaling, not generic spell levels.

entries.label: SSF
entries.statement: Viable after mandatory uniques; not a zero-gear league starter.

sections.note: Player reports are experience, not verified mechanics. Confirm exact scaling against the in-game tooltip.

items.question: Why does bossing need so many buttons?
answer: Mapping is automatic, but bosses need manual commands for burst and element switching. That is the designed split.

items.question: Is it a real summoner build?
answer: It commands Djinns and scales as minion/command damage, but you also act and issue commands — it is a hybrid, not a pure summoner.

items.question: Can I league-start it in SSF?
answer: Only after the mandatory unique pieces are secured. Verify which those are first.
